v.why: Filling an empty input-to-output edge with a skip adds a residual path to a deep conv cell, whereas replacing an existing conv/pool there only trades capacity.
Deleting the input-to-output residual skip harms trainability of the stacked network much more than deleting a shallow conv branch on that edge.
Removing a weak pooling edge costs little, while removing a 3x3 conv on edge 0 destroys the main deep path through node 1.
When node 1 feeds the output only via edge 2 (edge 4 absent), cutting edge 0 removes less useful computation than when node 1 also feeds the output directly.
Adding conv3x3 to an empty edge 0 revives node 1 and all its downstream edges, a far larger gain than upgrading an existing op there.
Adding a conv to a missing edge adds a new branch and capacity, whereas replacing skip/pool/1x1 on edge 1 yields only a marginal change.
Pooling on a previously empty edge adds a connection, while overwriting a conv on edge 2 with pooling removes depth and parameters.
Replacing the strongest op (conv3x3) with parameter-free pooling loses the most accuracy compared with replacing skip, 1x1, or none.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is identically zero, so a conv on edge 4 contributes nothing and the edit's benefit vanishes.
A skip on an empty edge 2 links node 1 to node 2 and deepens the cell, while replacing an existing conv3x3 with skip removes capacity.
